title: RAG Needs a Map: Using GraphRAG to Retrieve Connected Context — Nyah Macklin, Neo4j
talk_summary: A beginner-level Neo4j workshop introducing GraphRAG: building a knowledge graph from documents by LLM entity/relationship extraction guided by a fixed schema, then combining vector similarity search with Cypher graph traversal in an agent. Most of the talk is setup and product demo, but the schema-constrained extraction and vector+graph hybrid retrieval are copyable mechanisms.

takeaways.what_they_do: When building a knowledge graph from unstructured docs, they predefine allowed node types and relationship types and pass them to the LLM so it cannot invent new ones; the LLM can help draft the schema once, then it is fixed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: using that schema like that will guide the LLM so it won't just make up new node and relationship types. It'll stick to that.

takeaways.technique: Hybrid vector + graph retrieval for multi-hop and aggregation questions
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent tool does vector similarity search to find seed chunks, then a Cypher query traverses relationships from those nodes and returns nodes plus scores, so the LLM gets connected context instead of isolated chunks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need that cipher query to include nodes you can see here nodes and then scores as well

takeaways.technique: Graph for aggregation/counting queries instead of RAG
takeaways.what_they_do: They note vector RAG is bad at aggregation/concatenation across documents, and demonstrate answering 'how many lessons' via a graph count query rather than similarity search.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you're building out rag pipelines they're often pretty bad at doing this like I had mentioned this aggregation and concatenation piece
